name: faq-search

frames.best_why: Billing tab with 'plan' searched shows an open accordion answer, covering search, tabs and expansion together.

tagline: Searchable FAQ list with category tabs and expanding answers.
summary: A help-centre FAQ page with a live search box, underlined category tabs and a list of question rows that expand to reveal answers. Searching or filtering leaves either matching questions or a no-results state with a clear button.
appearance: A dark help page with a large Frequently Asked Questions heading, a grey intro line and a small pill search field. A row of underlined category labels sits over a stack of rounded bordered question rows, each ending in a chevron; an open row reveals a muted paragraph, and a footer invites contact.
behaviour: Typing in the search filters the questions live against titles and answers, and the category labels narrow the list to one topic with an underline on the active tab. Clicking a question expands its answer in place; when nothing matches, an empty state offers a Clear search button.
demo_content: Questions about creating a project, system requirements, collaboration, billing and bug reports.
use_when: A help centre needs a browsable, searchable list of questions that expand in place instead of separate pages.
avoid_when: The questions and answers are hardcoded in the file, with no deep links or pagination for a large knowledge base.
customise: There are no props: the questions, answers and categories are arrays inside the file, so content changes mean editing the source; colours follow the theme.
weight_why: A small list of questions with accordion transitions; no canvas or loops.

a11y.note: Accordion and tabs are keyboard reachable with good structure, but the search field relies on its placeholder for a name and reduced motion is not handled.

issues: The category tabs have no tab role or aria-selected, so the active tab is visual only.
The search field has a placeholder but no visible or aria label.
polish_why: Clean, well-spaced FAQ layout with working search; tab and search semantics are thin.
